dhk_grower.text: Carob syrup is the old sweetener of Cyprus: dark, thick and tasting a bit like toffee. My grandmother said it cured anything, and I've never proved her wrong.
The pods are ground to a flour, too. It tastes of chocolate and is much better for the teeth.

dhk_kafe.text: I've been at this table since 1998. They tried to move me once, but the table wouldn't go.
We play tavli here, which you'd call backgammon. The trick is to blame the dice and never your own wrist.

dhk_fisher.text: There are fewer fish than there used to be, but more of them in the right places. The bay's warm, and the sea bream like it.
The best catch of the year is always the one that got away. It's a very large fish by the end of the evening.

dhk_kid.text: My dad is in the Army and my mum is in the school. We've lived in Germany, Scotland and here. Here is the warmest.
I have a Cypriot friend named Andreas. We trade crisps for pastries every Friday. I'm getting the better deal.

dhk_peacekeeper.text: I'm stationed up the road, along the buffer zone. It's a quiet job, which is the idea.
Everything we do is meant to make sure the next day is the same as the last. It's the oddest kind of success.
